source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
The document's discussion section highlights that Kandal province farmers achieve notably better dried-kernel corn prices (averaging about 25% above the four-province sample average, i.e. around 792 riel/kg vs. the roughly 630 riel/kg dried-kernel average) while Battambang province farmers achieve prices around 9% below the sample average. It attributes this gap mainly to Kandal's proximity to Phnom Penh and better market access/transport infrastructure. However, it cautions that the price data comes from a relatively small, non-random sample and should not be treated as fully representative of provincial averages -- especially since not all price differences necessarily reflect quality differences; some may simply reflect which buyers happen to be operating in an area at a given time.

On seed cost: Kandal farmers were found to typically use hybrid seed at a rate of about 28 kg/ha costing around 23,000 riel/kg, while Battambang farmers used about 18 kg/ha of seed costing around 14,000 riel/kg -- reflecting both different seeding densities and different seed price points across the two provinces, likely tied to which seed varieties and sources (Vietnamese vs. Thai-sourced, or domestic reseller) are locally available.

On mechanization: use of farm machinery and processing equipment (e.g. for land preparation and shelling) also varies by province and is a source of production-cost variation, though the document notes this factor is under-studied and recommends further investigation into how machinery access could reduce production costs and improve consistency across provinces.
